title: Per-tenant micro-reservoir sampler with burst-aware admission and late-instrumentation to cut hot-path allocations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Several recent deploys (see incident links below) exposed tracing as a measurable contributor to p50/p95 latency and allocation pressure in high-QPS ingress services. Existing samplers either make sampling decisions too late (incurring allocations on every request) or rely on heavy-weight global reservoirs that are expensive to maintain per-tenant. Goal: reduce tracing hot-path allocations and CPU by moving to a compact, per-tenant micro-reservoir sampler with burst-aware admission and late-instrumentation. The sampler should decide acceptance on a tiny fast path (few branches, no heap allocs) and only attach/allocate full span objects when accepted. It should support short-lived burst elasticity so sudden tenant spikes don't OOM or swamp tracing backend, and a low-cost tail-detector to promote error/latency candidates for capture.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end median CPU/alloc per request reduced by >= 20% for instrumented ingress service under synthetic high-QPS workloads (see perf harness). 2) Traces submitted for errors and p99 latency are retained at >= 95% fidelity compared to baseline sampling. 3) No increase in end-to-end request latency p95 by more than 2ms at 95% confidence during canary. 4) Feature gated and toggleable per-tenant via Console rollout UI. 5) Observability: new metrics emitted (micro_reservoir.accepted, micro_reservoir.rejected_burst, micro_reservoir.promoted_tail, micro_reservoir.hotpath_alloc_reduction) and dashboards created for release.
plan: 1) Design: finalize fast-path admission algorithm and token header schema for propagation. 2) Prototype: implement in ingress-proxy (Go) with no-op spans until acceptance. 3) Async writer: reuse existing trace-writer but add batching window for micro-reservoir output. 4) Tail promotion: lightweight latency/error heuristic that triggers promotion without allocating full span on hot path. 5) Canary: enable for 5% of traffic in staging then prod with SLO guardrails. 6) Rollout and measure; iterate on admission and burst thresholds. 7) Docs: update SDK instrumentation guidance and Console toggle docs.
implementation_notes: - Use fixed-size ring buffer per tenant (micro-reservoir) stored in sharded in-memory map with eviction by age. - Admission decision uses tenant token + two 64-bit LCG counters to avoid atomic-heavy contention. - Late-instrumentation pattern: attach only a tiny opaque token to request context; allocate full span only on accept/promotion. - Burst handling: token bucket per-tenant with leaky window and backpressure counters emitted as metrics. - Promotion detector: service-level moving-window latency sketch + error-rate threshold to force capture. - Fallback: if tenant map unavailable, fall back to conservative global sampling config to avoid data loss.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: mis-tuned burst thresholds could drop important traces during real incidents. Mitigation: start with conservative thresholds and provide per-tenant override; expose a debug mode that forces capture for flagged requests. Risk: increased complexity may introduce regressions in proxy. Mitigation: thorough unit + load tests, CI perf regression checks, and staged canary rollout with automatic rollback on SLO triggers.
